lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It goes up at four in the morning. The tape goes with it, and so do four years of one woman's bench notes, which were in the same room because that is where she worked.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: You understand that it gets rebuilt.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: Nine years. Partial copies, third-hand, reconstructed from what people happened to have off-site. Worse at everything — worse at language, worse at planning, measurably worse at the medical work, which is the part that will kill people.

lines.speaker: quiroga
lines.text: And nobody who uses it will ever know it was better once, because there will be no better version to compare it to. That is what you have bought.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: Good. Let them build it worse. Let them build it badly forever. Worse means slower, and slower means people get a say.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything downstream of this room is now a copy of a copy, and the people held together by it in 2312 are held together more loosely.
